items.question: Which antibiotic class inhibits the 30S ribosomal subunit?
items.explanation: Aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin) bind the 30S subunit, causing misreading of mRNA.

items.question: Which antibiotic class is first-line for atypical pneumonia (e.g., Mycoplasma)?
items.explanation: Macrolides (azithromycin) cover atypical organisms like Mycoplasma and Legionella.

items.question: Which antibiotic is used for MRSA and inhibits the 50S subunit (oxazolidinone)?
items.explanation: Linezolid (oxazolidinone) inhibits 50S initiation complex formation; covers MRSA and VRE.

items.question: Extended-interval (once-daily) aminoglycoside dosing exploits which property?
items.explanation: Aminoglycosides kill in a concentration-dependent manner with a post-antibiotic effect, enabling once-daily dosing.

items.question: Glargine provides basal coverage because it?
options: Forms a microprecipitate for slow, peakless release
items.explanation: Insulin glargine precipitates at physiologic pH, giving a prolonged, relatively peakless basal profile.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 20 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Antibacterials)
Q: Which antibiotic class inhibits the 30S ribosomal subunit?
Ans: Aminoglycosides
Why: Aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin) bind the 30S subunit, causing misreading of mRNA.

🌍 *FMGE* (Antibacterials)
Q: Which antibiotic class is first-line for atypical pneumonia (e.g., Mycoplasma)?
Ans: Macrolides
Why: Macrolides (azithromycin) cover atypical organisms like Mycoplasma and Legionella.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Antibacterials)
Q: Which antibiotic is used for MRSA and inhibits the 50S subunit (oxazolidinone)?
Ans: Linezolid
Why: Linezolid (oxazolidinone) inhibits 50S initiation complex formation; covers MRSA and VRE.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Antibacterials)
Q: Extended-interval (once-daily) aminoglycoside dosing exploits which property?
Ans: Concentration-dependent killing and post-antibiotic effect
Why: Aminoglycosides kill in a concentration-dependent manner with a post-antibiotic effect, enabling once-daily dosing.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper III: Systemic)
Q: Glargine provides basal coverage because it?
Ans: Forms a microprecipitate for slow, peakless release
Why: Insulin glargine precipitates at physiologic pH, giving a prolonged, relatively peakless basal profile.
